## L1 Capability: Application Security

Application Security encompasses the enterprise-wide set of architectural capabilities required to ensure that software systems — across their full development and runtime lifecycle — are designed, built, deployed, and operated in a manner that protects confidentiality, integrity, and availability. As a domain within the enterprise security landscape, Application Security is distinct from Infrastructure Security (which governs platform and network controls), Identity Security (which governs authentication and access at the enterprise level), and Data Security (which governs data classification and protection at rest and in transit independent of application context). Application Security addresses the architectural concerns that arise specifically because software is authored, composed from third-party components, containerized, and exposed through APIs — concerns that cannot be fully addressed by infrastructure or identity controls alone.

## L2 Capability Areas

| L2 Capability | Description | Maturity |
|---|---|---|
| Secure Software Development | Architectural capabilities that embed security intent into the software development lifecycle — from threat modeling at design time through secure coding practices and pre-commit gate enforcement | Developing |
| API Security | Capabilities that protect the exposure, consumption, and lifecycle management of application programming interfaces, including authentication, authorization, traffic mediation, and schema validation at API boundaries | Developing |
| Application Security Testing | Capabilities that identify security weaknesses in application code and dependencies through automated static, dynamic, interactive, and composition analysis at appropriate stages of the development pipeline | Developing |
| Container & Image Security | Capabilities that govern the security posture of container images throughout their lifecycle — from build-time scanning and supply chain attestation through runtime behavioral enforcement | Developing |
| Container Orchestration Security | Capabilities that govern the security configuration and operational posture of container orchestration platforms, including control plane integrity, workload isolation, and policy enforcement at the orchestration layer | Developing |
| Database Security | Capabilities that protect data stored within enterprise database systems through architectural controls governing access patterns, activity visibility, and data confidentiality at the database tier | Developing |
| Web Application Protection | Capabilities that defend application-layer endpoints from exploitation at runtime — including traffic inspection, behavioral anomaly detection, and in-process self-protection mechanisms | Developing |
| Application Authentication & Authorization | Capabilities that establish and enforce identity assertions and access decisions within and between application components, distinct from enterprise identity governance | Developing |
| Secrets Management | Capabilities that govern the lifecycle of application credentials, cryptographic keys, tokens, and other sensitive configuration values — including secure storage, controlled distribution, and automated rotation | Developing |
| Software Supply Chain Security | Capabilities that establish and maintain the integrity and provenance of software components, build artifacts, and dependencies throughout the software supply chain | Initial |

## Scope and Boundaries

**In Scope**: Architectural capabilities that apply to software systems authored, assembled, or operated by the enterprise — including internally developed applications, containerized workloads, APIs, and the pipelines that build and deliver them.

**Out of Scope**:
- Enterprise identity governance and workforce access management (see Identity Security capability domain)
- Network-layer security controls (see Network Security capability domain)
- Infrastructure platform hardening (see Cloud & Infrastructure Security capability domain)
- Data classification and data lifecycle governance independent of application context (see Data Security capability domain)
- Endpoint security (see Endpoint Security capability domain)
- Security monitoring, detection, and response (see SecOps capability domain)
- Enforceable security standards and control baselines — those are maintained in `standards/security/`

**Non-ABB Guardrail**: This document defines capabilities at L1/L2 only. Architecture Building Blocks, solution patterns, security controls, vendor selections, and compliance requirements are explicitly out of scope for this artifact.
